newsitem.title: USA: CBOT CORN ENDS HIGHER ON SHORT COVERING.
newsitem.headline: CBOT CORN ENDS HIGHER ON SHORT COVERING.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on short covering before the weekend, traders said.
"It was just a trading day. There was pre-weekend trading and Monday probably will be a reduced volume before Tuesday's crop report," said Dave Armstrong, analyst for ABN Amro, The Chicago Corp.

Corn futures fell hard Thursday on some outlooks for rain this weekend in dry areas of the U.S. Midwest. Those forecasts remain intact but there are some outlooks that indicate only minimal amounts of rain for that portion of the Midwest that most needs the moisture.
Two storm systems will bring chances for rain to the U.S. Midwest this weekend but Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said amounts would likely remain under one inch.
Corn closed 1-1/4 to five cents per bushel higher, with September up 3-1/2 at $2.53-1/2.
The market took note of a corn crop estimate revealed early Friday by the Conrad Leslie-ADM Elevator group.
Leslie pegged 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.656 billion bushels, above an average analysts' estimate of 9.554 billion bushels but below USDA's July forecast for 9.7 billion bushels.
USDA at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT Tuesday will release its August crop production and supply/demand reports.

In spread dealings, ADM Investor Services did 2.5 million bushels of December/March at 8-1/2 to 8-1/4 cents, premium March, traders said. Cargill Inc did two million May/December at 13 to 13-1/2 cents and FIMAT Futures spread 1.5 million December/September at three cents, traders said.

Cargill Inc sold four million bushels of September, Cargill Investor Services bought two million bushels of December and sold one million and Griffin Trading bought one million December and sold two million December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 47,500 contracts, below the 65,173 traded Thursday.

In corn options, Griffin Trading bought 500 December $3.00 calls at three cents, Continental Grain bought 800 December $2.60 calls at 11-3/4 cents and sold 800 December $3.00 calls at three cents, traders said. Continental also bought 800 December $2.60 calls at 11-1/2 cents and sold 800 December $3.00 calls at three cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, below the 28,006 traded Thursday.
